Meaning in this study: Reported load minus reported wind and solar generation, with provider specific accounting boundaries.
Seasonal monitoring levels estimated from permitted previous observations. They are statistical exceedance targets, not adequacy limits.
At least two of the three monitored areas exceed their own level in the same UTC hour.
Mean squared difference between the issued event probability and its binary outcome. Lower is better; it measures probability loss rather than dispatch cost.
Probability integral transform: the observed value evaluated in its issued marginal CDF. It diagnoses marginal forecast calibration.
A dependence model joining marginal forecast distributions into a multivariate distribution.
Student t degrees of freedom. The tested finite values change dependence shape; infinity is the Gaussian limit.
Original issued margins with weather conditioned Gaussian dependence.
Additional conditional marginal map with the same Gaussian dependence.
Original margins with event selected, shared R Student t dependence.
Additional conditional marginal map with the same selected t dependence.
Compulsory top two probability hours in each complete 24 hour UTC target day window.
At most two hours above or at the probability gate; zero hours are allowed.
Gated risk rise priority with a cooldown and at most two selected hours per UTC day.
One selected target hour for follow up review. It does not measure staffing time or an implemented dispatch action.
Consecutive active event days, with the specified allowance for inactive days; missing days split spells.
At least one selected true event target hour in the first six elapsed hours after realised spell onset. Forecasts were already issued; onset does not trigger a warning.
Analytic retained hit probability after uniform, label blind sampling of the same total number of slots from each rule. This is evaluation standardisation, not a prospective annual budget controller.
